description:
Glass Insulator Lot - 3 Pieces
Hemingray and American Manufactured
Aqua Teal and Clear, Vintage Mid-Century Era
This collection of three vintage glass insulators represents a significant era in American telecommunications history. Used primarily to insulate telegraph and telephone wires from their wooden support poles, these heavy glass pieces are prized by collectors for their industrial aesthetic and vibrant glass colors. This lot provides a balanced display including a classic aqua teal piece and two clear glass specimens.
Pieces Included:
Hemingray Insulator, Aqua Teal Glass, embossed "HEMINGRAY" with beaded drip points - minor base fleabites
Clear Glass Insulator, embossed "MADE IN U.S.A.", smooth base - excellent vintage condition

description:
Hemingray Glass Company
No. 45 Glass Insulator
Pressed Glass, Clear, Vintage
A classic piece of American industrial history, this Hemingray No. 45 glass insulator was a standard component for telegraph and telephone lines during the 20th century. These insulators are sought after by collectors for their sculptural form and historical significance in the expansion of communication infrastructure. The No. 45 model features a robust double-petticoat design intended for high-performance electrical isolation.
Double petticoat construction for electrical insulation integrity
Clear glass with a subtle light aqua tint characteristic of period glass production
Embossed "HEMINGRAY - 45" marking prominently on the lower base skirt
Approximately 3.75 inch base diameter and 4 inch total height
Condition:
Excellent vintage condition with no major chips or structural cracks. Inner and outer petticoats are intact. Original gloss is well-preserved with minor surface scratches consistent with age and utility service. Threaded core is clean and undamaged.

shipping.policy:
Payment:
The only methods of payment we accept are Visa, Master Card, and Discover Card. We do not accept cash, checks, or any other form of payment.
Sales tax will be figured and added to each purchase based on the rate and requirement from your state.
Shipping:
Upon receipt of payment, we utilize Fedex and USPS as our primary shipping carriers. Shipments to P.O. Boxes will be shipped by USPS. We do our best to have items shipped within 7 business days from the date of payment; we are not open on weekends. We are limited to the carriers’ rules and regulations when shipping an order. Shipping charges are calculated at time of payment. Please check shipping rates prior to placing your bid. All items will be shipped as listed and will not be dismantled for any reason.
Minimum shipment weight is 1 lb. Items weighing less than 1 lb. will be calculated at the 1 lb. rate.
Please check shipping rates prior to placing your bid.
Combined Orders:
Multiple items can be combined PRIOR TO the checkout process provided that the payment deadline has not expired on any of the items that you are combining to create the order, and that the combined weight does not exceed 20 pounds. Combined shipping must be requested by the customer prior to payment; it is not automatically allowed. Once an item has been paid for, it is no longer eligible for combined shipping. We reserve the right to deny combination of certain items.
Insurance:
Buyer must email a request for insurance prior to making payment. Insurance cannot be added by the buyer during the payment process. An e-mail must be sent to us and we will then edit the order total for you.
We apologize, but if your package is damaged or lost we will not be able to issue a refund unless your package was insured. We strongly recommend insurance on all breakable items. Photos will be required before a refund will be considered.
Handling Fee:
A minimum of $3.00 handling fee will appear at checkout and applies to all purchases regardless of delivery method or pick up. Our handling fee is a set fee and cannot be adjusted. (Certain items that are very fragile, irregularly shaped, and/or heavy may be subject to an increased handling fee.) These fees, along with your purchase, help to support our Goodwill mission.

Lilla Clasica Handmade Tobacco Pipe
Hand-Carved Wooden Pipe with Decorative Accents
Wood, Feathers, and Beads, Approximately 16 Inches Long
A fine hand-made tobacco pipe from the Lilla Clasica collection, featuring a long, elegant churchwarden-style silhouette. This piece combines traditional woodworking with ornamental indigenous-inspired aesthetics, making it a striking display piece or a unique addition to a pipe collection. The pipe is presented in its original satin-lined gift box, highlighting its status as a crafted specialty item.
Hand-carved wooden bowl with a textured, scale-like pattern and deep polished finish
Extra-long wooden stem terminating in a black tapered mouthpiece
Decorative cord wrap adorned with natural-toned beads and dark brown feathers
Includes original maroon presentation box with a gold-tone brand logo and yellow satin lining
Approximately 16 inches in total length
Condition:
The pipe is in excellent condition and appears unsmoked, with no residue or charring inside the bowl. The wood finish remains bright and glossy across both the bowl and stem. Decorative feathers and beads are fully intact and securely attached. The presentation box is structurally sound with minor shelf wear on the exterior; the interior lining is clean and vibrant.

When an order includes both flat-rate and dimensional-weight items, shipping may be calculated using dimensional weight. Combining these items does not necessarily reduce shipping costs and may result in the same or higher shipping charges than purchasing them separately.

The specimens vary in size and form a diverse collection of geological and paleontological samples.

title: Hemingray 42 Glass Insulator Set 2 Aqua Blue Green CD 154 Made in USA Vintage
description:
Hemingray Glass Company Set - 2 Pieces
Hemingray 42 (CD 154)
Aqua, Vintage Mid-Century
This set features two vintage aqua glass insulators produced by the Hemingray Glass Company, identified by the "Hemingray-42" mold mark. The No. 42 model, classified as CD 154 by collectors, was one of the most widely used designs for telephone and telegraph lines across North America during the early-to-mid 20th century. Prized for their deep aqua color and iconic industrial aesthetic, these pieces represent a significant era of American telecommunications history and are staple items for glass insulator collectors.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Condition:
Both insulators are in good vintage condition with characteristic wear expected from outdoor utility use. The glass retains high clarity and its original vibrant aqua hue. As is common with authentic vintage insulators, there are minor fleabites and small chips along the sharp drip points on the beaded base. No large structural cracks or major damage to the wire grooves or top domes observed.

Late 20th Century, 1 Pen with Case
Paradise Pens of Hawaii specializes in writing instruments crafted from native Hawaiian hardwoods, emphasizing the natural beauty of the island's flora. This ballpoint pen is fashioned from Koa wood, a species endemic to the Hawaiian Islands that was historically reserved for Hawaiian monarchs. The warm, chatoyant grain of the Koa is complemented by gold-tone accents, reflecting the brand's commitment to Hawaiian craftsmanship and environmental reforestation projects.
Case label identifies manufacturer and "KOA" wood material origin
